item.title: Trump Switched to Old Air Force One at NATO Summit After Credible Iranian Threat
item.description: The threat led the Secret Service to urge President Trump to fly out of Turkey on the old plane, raising questions about the security of the Qatari-donated jet.
item.dc:creator: Tyler Pager, Julian E. Barnes and Maggie Haberman
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)
item.media:description: President Trump walking off the older Air Force One at Mildenhall Air Force Base in Britain on July 8. He swapped to the newer jet, donated by Qatar, for the flight back to Washington.

item.title: Iran’s New Leader Is More Open to Pursuing a Nuclear Weapon, U.S. Intelligence Says
item.description: The previous supreme leader, who was killed early in the war, had renounced nuclear weapons. U.S. spy agencies believe his son is more interested in building a bomb.
item.dc:creator: Julian E. Barnes
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)
item.media:credit: Arash Khamooshi/Polaris for The New York Times
item.media:description: A billboard in Tehran of Iran’s three supreme leaders, including Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei at right. A determination that he is potentially open to pursuing a bomb would provide additional justification for an escalation of the Trump administration’s military campaign.

item.title: Cornell, Northwestern and Other Universities Plan for Classes at Middle East Campuses
item.description: Even after the collapse of the cease-fire between the United States and Iran, American universities expect to teach in Qatar and the United Arab Emirates, and a new outpost is on track to open in Saudi Arabia.
item.dc:creator: Alan Blinder
item.media:credit: Bernd von Jutrczenka/Picture-Alliance/DPA, via Associated Press Images
item.media:description: The University of New Haven is still planning to inaugurate its new campus in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia.

item.title: Opposing Defense Bill, Democrats Shift Their Tactics
item.description: Crossing what was once seen as a political red line, Democrats voted against the usually bipartisan measure, registering dissent about the war in Iran.
item.dc:creator: Carl Hulse
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)
United States Defense and Military Forces
item.media:description: Senator Angus King, a Maine independent, this month opposed the annual Pentagon policy measure for the first time.

item.title: The Artist Matthew Taylor Is Helping Trump Reshape Washington
item.description: Matthew Taylor, a conceptual artist and political strategist, made influential ads and documentaries produced by Steve Bannon. Now he’s assisting the White House.
item.dc:creator: Zachary Small
item.media:description: Matthew Taylor, a senior adviser at the National Endowment for the Humanities, has an artistic background that makes him a distinct champion of the president’s vision.

item.title: Trump Administration Admits Canceling Grants to States That Did Not Vote for Him
item.description: Federal officials said in court documents that they halted billions of dollars in funding for energy projects to states “based solely” on whether they backed President Trump in the 2024 election.
item.dc:creator: Tony Romm and Brad Plumer
item.media:description: Russell Vought, director of the Office of Management and Budget, last month.

item.title: Paramount Agrees to Delay Warner Bros. Merger for Months
item.description: The company agreed to a proposed freeze until June 2027, unless a judge issues a ruling before then on a lawsuit blocking the deal.
item.dc:creator: Benjamin Mullin, David McCabe and Lauren Hirsch
item.media:credit: Ricardo Nagaoka for The New York Times
item.media:description: The merger would unite two major movie studios and several streaming services.

item.title: Measles Cases Hit New Record in U.S., as Vaccination Rates Wane
item.description: More measles cases have been reported in the United States in the last two years than in all the years from 2000 through 2024 combined.
item.dc:creator: Teddy Rosenbluth
item.category: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
item.media:description: A patient with measles symptoms in South Carolina in January.

item.title: C.D.C. Expands Cyclospora Outbreak Linked to Iceberg Lettuce to Nine States
item.description: Illinois, Kansas, Oklahoma and Pennsylvania now join Michigan, Ohio, Indiana, Kentucky and West Virginia in cyclospora outbreak linked to iceberg lettuce.
item.dc:creator: Alice Callahan and Caroline Hopkins Legaspi
item.category: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

item.title: F.D.A. Panel’s Vote on Peptides Raises Concerns About a Prescribing Boom
item.description: The committee endorsed broader use of the peptides in lightly regulated compounding pharmacies that have grown into a multibillion-dollar business.
item.dc:creator: Christina Jewett and Dana G. Smith
item.media:credit: Andrew Mangum for The New York Times
item.media:description: Some F.D.A. scientists pointed out that the peptides under review had not been proven to be safe or effective, and could present risks to patients.

item.title: Wildfires in France and Spain Drive Tens of Thousands From Their Homes
item.description: French officials ordered the evacuation of the Cap Ferret Peninsula, a popular holiday destination. Fires west of Madrid were closing in on populated areas.
item.dc:creator: Carlos Barragán
item.media:description: On the beach in Lacanau in southwestern France on Friday.

item.title: Faced With Heat and Wildfires, France Turns to Spain to Learn How to Cope
item.description: A French government delegation will travel to its southern neighbor to learn how it copes with long spells of hot weather.
item.dc:creator: Mark Landler
item.media:credit: Dmitry Kostyukov for The New York Times
item.media:description: Trying to stay cool in Paris during a heat wave last month.

item.title: Crucial Interest Rate Jumps to Highest Level of Trump’s Second Term
item.description: The yield on the 10-year Treasury bond has risen steadily this year, as the Iran war rages, government spending worries intensify and artificial intelligence spending boosts growth.
item.dc:creator: Joe Rennison and Gregory Schmidt
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)
item.media:description: Scott Bessent, the U.S. Treasury secretary, has previously pointed to the yield on the 10-year Treasury bond as a “barometer” of his success in improving affordability.

item.title: As Canada Opens Gordie Howe International Bridge, Americans Are Told to Stay Home
item.description: After a delay ordered by President Trump and new tariffs against Canada, the bridge between Windsor, Ontario, and Detroit finally opened on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Ian Austen
item.category: Gordie Howe International Bridge (Detroit, Mich and Windsor, Ontario)
item.media:description: The Gordie Howe International Bridge in Windsor, Ontario, officially opened on Friday.

item.title: Small Businesses Sue Trump Administration Over Latest Tariffs
item.description: The businesses are represented by the Liberty Justice Center, a legal group that has successfully challenged President Trump’s past duties.
item.dc:creator: Tony Romm and Ana Swanson
item.media:credit: Maggie Shannon for The New York Times
item.media:description: Asher Rapkin, an owner of Collective Horology, re-sizing a watch at his office in Ventura, Calif. His company is suing the Trump administration over the new tariffs.

item.title: Trump Tariff Fight Stalls Russia Sanctions Bill Championed by Lindsey Graham
item.description: A bipartisan bill championed by the late Senator Lindsey Graham has become mired in a dispute over expanding President Trump’s tariff power.
item.dc:creator: Robert Jimison
item.media:description: President Trump has pushed aggressively to go around Congress and move unilaterally to shield the U.S. economy from foreign competition with tariffs.

item.title: After the Cesar Chavez Scandal, Can Johnny Itliong Restore His Father’s Activist Legacy?
item.description: Johnny Itliong says Cesar Chavez stole credit from his father, the farmworker activist Larry Itliong. For years, he has been trying to correct the record.
item.dc:creator: Jill Cowan and Mark Abramson for The New York Times
item.media:description: “I have been fighting to get the story of my father out for decades and have been waiting for the U.F.W. to step up and honor Larry as they do Cesar,” said Johnny Itliong, at a mural commemorating his father.

item.title: Argentines Facing Surge of Criticism After World Cup Loss Have Something to Say
item.description: Many Argentines condemned their players’ racist chants and aggressive behavior during the World Cup, but rejected what felt like a sweeping stigmatization of their entire nation.
item.dc:creator: Emma Bubola and Daniel Politi
item.media:credit: Sebastián López Brach for The New York Times
item.media:description: Argentine supporters at the National Flag Memorial in Rosario, Argentina, after the World Cup final on Sunday.

item.title: Car Condos Give Your Vehicle Luxury Housing
item.description: No longer satisfied by regular parking garages, some drivers are upgrading their luxury vehicles’ homes.
item.dc:creator: Jessica Shaw

item.title: Democrats Vote to Put South Carolina First in 2028 Primary
item.description: Along with Nevada, New Hampshire, New Mexico, Michigan and Virginia, the state will help decide the party’s next presidential nominee.
item.dc:creator: Shane Goldmacher and Aishvarya Kavi
item.media:description: South Carolina moved to the front of the Democratic presidential nominating calendar for the 2024 election under the Biden administration.

item.title: What We Know About the Police Shooting in Madison
item.description: A Black man was shot and killed by the police on Wednesday, not far from the Wisconsin Capitol. An investigation is underway.
